Reducing spasticity can have a positive impact on arm function. A targeted meta-analytic approach has demonstrated that this is the case. This means that by focusing specifically on patients with arm spasticity, healthcare providers can show significant improvements in their overall mobility and ability to perform daily activities.

In contrast, reducing cardiac reoperations in octogenarians is not necessarily beneficial. While these surgeries may offer a sense of independence and satisfaction, they are often accompanied by high perioperative mortality rates, which highlights the importance of careful consideration when deciding whether such interventions are warranted.
